key_insight: The paper shows that robust learning under Wasserstein DRO can be framed as learning transport maps, and that the optimal adversary must satisfy cyclical monotonicity, which standard per-sample adversarial training generally breaks.
engineering_relevance: For safety-critical ML, this suggests more principled adversarial training methods that better match worst-case distribution shifts and can improve robustness without unnecessary perturbation cost.
method: Reformulate the DRO adversary as a transport-map optimization problem over sample moves.
Use multi-start particle ascent with reassignment to enforce cyclical monotonicity across samples.
Parameterize adversarial maps as gradients of input-convex neural networks to guarantee monotone transport by design.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments on robust regression, image classification, and robust control, where the proposed methods outperform standard adversarial training and strong baselines on robustness and generalization under distribution shift.
watch_item: The proposed methods add optimization and modeling complexity, so stable training and scalability to large high-dimensional problems may require careful implementation and tuning.
paper_title: Brenier Meets Adversarial Training: Optimal Transport Geometry for Robust Learning
